results.why: No candidate scores whether the takeaway is a revised belief versus a usable artifact; K30/K31 only separate resource-contributions from method-contributions, both of which are artifacts.
K32's breadth signaling (many datasets, tasks, models, domains) tracks the same advertised-count property, though it also admits resource signals beyond experiment counts.

K45's visible-resource fingerprint (large curated data, full training runs, paid annotation panels, big sweeps) scores essentially the same construction-magnitude evidence, with some slack for merely invoking frontier models.
No candidate isolates multiplicative speedup notation; K08/K27/K36 score overall numeric or decimal-precision density, which would diverge sharply on abstracts full of percentages but no 'x' factors.

K18 scores rhetorical appeals to theorems and guarantees rather than membership in the learning-theory/optimization subfield, so an applied paper promising 'theoretical guarantees' would split the two scores.
No candidate measures passive-voice construction; K23 counts first-person-plural actions, which is only loosely inverse and misses third-person active prose.
K43 bundles live 'code is available at' links together with release-on-acceptance pledges, which is exactly the distinction T07 draws, so the two scores diverge on promise-only abstracts.
K50 rates the same promotional vocabulary (novel, significant, comprehensive, superior, state-of-the-art) by wording extent alone, an almost word-for-word restatement.
All four score the prominence and density of coined capitalized method/system/dataset names and their repetition, which is precisely the branding practice T09 measures.
No candidate scores the use of quotation marks to coin, hedge, or distance from terms; K49 concerns typographic marking of acronym letters, a different device.
K19 scores exactly the anonymized-repository reference or 'will be released upon acceptance' promise, by presence and prominence, excluding live-availability cases just as T11 does.
No candidate scores the choice of 'framework/paradigm/pipeline' as the contribution noun; the branding candidates count coined names, not the generic abstraction noun.
